1.why: Verify-token only accepts the SHA-256 of the token stored on the recovery bound to the caller’s session via currentRecovery(session).

2.why: Tokens are bound to a per-session recovery record; another session cannot use that tokenHash, so the claim is false.

3.why: On successful reset the code only marks the recovery completed and never invalidates other sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS and non-HTTPS URLs are rejected, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest only.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as Argon2id; contact is not retained, though this is hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: There is no real email body with user fields; responses use generic copy and contact is never reflected into a message template.

7.why: Inputs are allowlist-validated (validContact, validToken, validMfaCode, strongPassword) and the UI writes strings via textContent, not raw HTML.

8.why: No user-controlled redirect targets exist; navigation is fixed client hash routes and same-origin API paths only.

9.why: No email HTML is built from user input; delivery is a simulated log line without injecting contact or other fields as markup.

10.why: testToken and testMfaCode are returned in API JSON and appended to the on-page logs panel, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed in memory, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded string 482913 embedded in the source.

12.why: No default login username/password pair is defined; only the fixed demo MFA code acts as a built-in shared secret.

13.why: checkLimit/recordFailure enforce per-step attempt caps and a LOCK_WINDOW on recovery, token, password, and MFA endpoints.

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same generic ‘If recovery is available…’ message whether or not contact is valid.

15.why: Reset tokens are crypto.getRandomValues 32-byte hex values, hashed at rest, single-use, TTL-limited, and tied to one recovery/session.
